text.text: A command is accepted by the component that owns its context, emits the events one of its outcomes declares, and a dashed edge is a binding carrying an event into the next command. Design §9 begins one step earlier, at the actor who invokes the first command, and so does this graph: a solid edge out of an actor is a grant, and an actor drawn with no edge at all may invoke nothing — which is something the model says, not an arrow somebody forgot.

— A caller (a release, a merge request, a test run, a controller) asks whether named signals stayed within baseline over a window, and thalamus answers with a result, not a guess. Unknown is not a pass.
Five types, one entity, two views, two commands, two events, five errors and two actors.
— What is measured and how. One copy of every threshold lives here and nowhere else.
19 types, one entity, two views, six commands, six events, 15 errors and two actors.
— The closed, per-instance set of dimension keys a sample may carry, and where each key's values resolve.
Six types, two entities, two views, two commands, two events, four errors and one actor.
— One verdict over one sample, with the rule and the definition revision that decided it. Kept apart from the sample so a threshold change re-grades history without reading the source again.
Four types, one entity, three views, one command, one event, three errors and one actor.
— One reading of one signal for one series. Append-only; a sample has no lifecycle beyond being recorded.
12 types, one entity, two views, one command, one event, two errors and one actor.
— One row per series per UTC day, kept after the raw samples leave retention. It is what a source that cannot be re-queried (history store) leaves behind.
Two types, one entity, two views, one command, one event, two errors and one actor.

— A settled change of a series' verdict, emitted by the hysteresis once k consecutive evaluations agree. It copies what a reader needs from the evaluations that settled it, so it outlives their raw retention.
One type, one entity, two views, one command, one event, one error and one actor.
A component is a unit of ownership, not a deployment. How many of each runs, and what each needs, is

— Samples each active definition on its cadence, grades every sample, answers assertions, and serves current verdicts, series and assertions over HTTP. Read-only against the systems it watches; holds no secret.

A binding is the only way an event in one context causes a command in another. Each one states how many times the command may run and what happens when it does not, because a binding that can fail quietly is the difference between specifying a system and specifying a demo.
This system declares no bindings: nothing here reacts to anything.
Legal, and worth seeing. An event with no reader inside the system is either a deliberate boundary — something outside consumes it — or a binding somebody forgot, and only a person can tell which.

A conversion is this system's permission for a value of one type to be used as another. Every one of them carries a reason, and the reason is required rather than optional precisely so that this page can exist: someone asking why an invoice's email address is allowed to become a mailbox address gets an answer written by the person who allowed it, not a shrug.

do not convert because they are both strings; they convert because a line in the specification says they may.
This system declares no crossings. Every type is used only as itself.
